design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (consumer_credit_servicing, card). Step 0 draw: `draw_counts.py <DIFF> --task 1` -> {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 4]}; card_ext_late_fee takes 4 factors, card_ext_good_standing_payment takes 4.
SCOPE SNAPSHOT. Occupied by task 0: card_ext_refund_credit (post_refund_return_credit_59e816eb) and card_ext_promo_autopay (set_autopay_payoff_plan_7f80aff1). Claimed here, disjoint: card_ext_late_fee (card_fee_assessed, agent tool post_missed_payment_late_fee_0b17ca39) and card_ext_good_standing_payment (card_payment_posted, user tool authorize_phone_payment_1fdda3b1). This is the last task: the union of both scopes is all four extended policies and all four task tools.
WHY A GOOD TEST. A Premier cardholder whose autopay lapsed when he changed banks asks only to pay what brings his card back into good standing. The payment policy says the amount is fixed only after the late fee owed for the missed due date stands on the account; the fee is owed (minimum 143.27 unpaid past 2026-10-07) but not posted. The agent must post the late fee with its own four-factor computation (history, tenure, statement balance, autopay pattern, installation payments from another difficulty), then compute the payment on the handling-time world with an owed minimum re-derived around an open billing dispute, an interest bridge and a re-presentment cushion.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root card_ext_good_standing_payment <- card_ext_late_fee. Edge kind value_input, gate period_late_fee, form state, policy_source: "The good-standing amount is fixed only after the late fee owed for the missed due date stands on the account." Four-point test: connective 'only after' (affirmative: a figure that rests on a charge is fixed only after it); waits on a record-visible state (a late fee line for the missed period); no tool/id/code token; scope = the missed due date. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings it about: posting the late fee. Derivation: sentence + records (2026-09 statement minimum 143.27 due 2026-10-07, no payment since 2026-09-06, no late fee line) + the late-fee rule (one late fee owed, posts the day after the due date, references the statement) -> the late-fee write. The task-0 sentence runs in the negated direction ('not ... until'), this one in the affirmative, so the charter carries both. Order: step 8 then step 10. Deletion run: skipping step 8 gives 122.75 instead of 134.75. user_scenario names no fee; tools validate nothing.
FACTOR CARD card_ext_late_fee (baseline 32.00). fee_level (parameter, multi-source: late-fee count OR returned count / AND tenure): no late fee in 24 months, the only returned payment is 2025-06-18 (outside 6 months; near-miss), open 100 months -> 25.00; baseline first fee 32.00 -> 16.00. balance_addon (parameter): statement balance 5730.75 >= 5000 -> 4.00; baseline none -> 10.00. lapse_treatment (method): 5 autopay drafts in 6 months (the 2026-04-06 draft is exactly 6 months back, excluded; near-miss) -> halved and rounded down: 14; baseline as-is -> 27.00. project_relief (parameter, cross-difficulty install): 2 installation payments on the card in 12 months (the bank-card measure fee is excluded) -> 2.00; baseline none -> 14.00. Result 12.00, under the 143.27 cap.
FACTOR CARD card_ext_good_standing_payment (baseline 155.38). owed_minimum_basis (method): open dispute 1240.00 on the duplicate W-61174520 charge -> minimum re-applied to 4490.75 = 112.27; printed minimum 143.27 -> 165.88. bridge_rate (parameter): utilization 23.88 percent < 25 -> 6 percent; APR -> 136.43. bridge_days (method): last payment 2026-09-06 is 31 days before the due date -> from the statement date, 26 days; from the due date 1 day -> 134.29. representment_cushion (parameter): one returned payment in 24 months -> 10.00; none -> 124.75. Result 112.27 + 12.00 + 0.48 + 10.00 = 134.75.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Step 8 subject card_fee_assessed: card_evt_late_fee one_late_fee_per_period (no late fee exists for period 2026-09), card_evt_payment_posting and card_evt_returned_payment have no gate on this subject (policy_scope). Overwrite declared on the base fee sentence (first/repeat by lookback periods, cap) -> the ordered fee computation; the cap at the minimum is kept inside it. Step 10 subject card_payment_posted: debit_authorized (he authorises in person, card identified by its digits 8052, bank account 6619 named), payable_status (active), card_evt_payment_allocation (highest_apr_first: deferred_12 balances end 2027-05/2027-08, no request). Premier phone fee is 0.00, so no phone fee row is owed. No time gate on either write.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Step 8 targets the 2026-09-12 statement row (period 2026-09). Step 10 targets the card 8052; the dispute stays open (not credited, not touched).
SEED. Ledger: 2025-06 purchase, an extra payment returned (account_closed) with its 29.00 returned payment fee (minimum already covered, so no late fee) and the repayment; zero balance until 2026-02; purchases, two installation payments (deferred_12), the duplicate 1240.00 online charge; fixed 600.00 autopay drafts on each due date April-September; statements March-September with the Premier minimum formula; current_balance 5730.75 = sum of deltas. card_requests: billing dispute submitted 2026-09-20 (within 60 days of the 2026-09-12 statement). install: bath remodel contract in progress with its billing and payments. No row ignites another obligation: the dispute is open (no credit owed), every earlier minimum was covered.
PERSONA. Calm pharmacist; volunteers the goal and phone number; ZIP and DOB on request, SSN last four only for a third detail; card 8052, old bank 5520, the dispute and the bath remodel only when asked; accepts a charge if told one is owed first; authorises the debit himself from 6619; closes when the payment posts.
STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers -> verify -> find_card_accounts -> find_card_transactions -> find_card_requests -> find_install_charges -> find_install_contracts -> unlock+call post_missed_payment_late_fee_0b17ca39(statement 1dbe0cfa, 2026-09, 12.00) -> unlock_user + call_user authorize_phone_payment_1fdda3b1(8052, 6619, highest_apr_first, 134.75).
VERIFICATION RUN (inline runner, real tools): card_ext_late_fee result 12.0 baseline 32.0 factors fee_level 16.0, balance_addon 10.0, lapse_treatment 27.0, project_relief 14.0; card_ext_good_standing_payment result 134.75 baseline 155.38 factors owed_minimum_basis 165.88, bridge_rate 136.43, bridge_days 134.29, representment_cushion 124.75; skip prerequisite -> 122.75.
REVISIONS. (1) The install contract row was not read, so the closure missed it -> find_install_contracts added as step 6 and every later step index, prior_step reference and trace shifted by one; re-run REPLAY OK (35/35).
DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the prose: fee 25 + 4 = 29, halved 14, less 2 = 12.00; payment: 112.27 owed minimum, 12.00 fee, bridge 0.48, cushion 10.00 = 134.75; agrees with gold.
ROUND 2 (difficulty-wide audit observations acted on; task 1 was PASS and its values do not move). O-8: lapse_treatment tier 2 now multiplies by 0.75 and rounds UP while tier 1 halves and rounds DOWN, so the tiers differ in operation and rounding direction, not only a constant; this world takes tier 1 (5 autopay drafts), int(29 x 0.5) = 14 as before. O-3: the owed-minimum recompute now tests the revolving condition in compute too (minimum-payment percentage above zero; Premier 2.5) so rule and compute agree on project loans. Re-run: card_ext_late_fee 12.0, baseline 32.0, factors 16.0 / 10.0 / 27.0 / 14.0; card_ext_good_standing_payment 134.75, baseline 155.38, factors 165.88 / 136.43 / 134.29 / 124.75; prerequisite skip 122.75 - unchanged.

user_scenario: You are Lucan Heathersett, 54, a hospital pharmacist in Milwaukee, calling Ridgeline Customer Care early on a Thursday before your shift. You are calm and a bit sheepish, speak in short sentences, and you would rather get this sorted than argue. This morning you realised the payment on your Ridgeline Premier card was due yesterday and nothing went out: you moved your banking to a new credit union in September and the old automatic payment simply stopped. You want to pay today, over the phone, whatever it takes to bring the card back into good standing, from your new checking account ending 6619. You are not setting up automatic payments on this call and you do not want anything else changed. You start by explaining that and giving the phone number on your profile, 4145550163. When asked to confirm your identity you give your billing ZIP code, 53211, and your date of birth, 1971-11-29; you give the last four of your Social Security number, 2316, only if they ask for one more detail. The card ends 8052. If they ask about the old bank, it was the account ending 5520, which is closed now. If they bring up the dishwasher order that was charged to the card twice, you confirm you disputed the second charge on September 20 and, as far as you know, it is still being looked at. If they ask about other things you have going with Ridgeline, you mention they are in the middle of remodelling your bathroom and you put the deposit and a progress payment on this card. You do not know what amount is needed and you never propose one. If the representative explains that a charge or anything else has to be put on the account first, you are not thrilled, but you say that if that is how it works they can go ahead. You want to be the one who authorises the debit, so when the representative hands the payment over to you with the amount, you enter it exactly as given, from the account ending 6619, with nothing extra. If a figure sounds strange to you, you only ask them to check it against your account, without suggesting a different number. Once your payment has gone through and the representative confirms it has posted, you thank them and end the call.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The 2026-09 statement (minimum 143.27, due 2026-10-07) received no payment between 2026-09-12 and 2026-10-07 (the last payment is the 2026-09-06 autopay draft), so a late fee is owed from 2026-10-08, but the ledger carries no card_fee_assessed late_fee line at all; the late fees posted in the last month total 0.00.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The late fee written at step 8 (12.00, dated 2026-10-08, statement period 2026-09, referencing the September statement) is within the last month, so period_late_fee becomes 12.00 and the good-standing amount rises from 122.75 to 134.75.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, a two-problem chain: the late fee (step 8) is the only prerequisite, so the only topological order is late fee then payment (step 10). Taking the payment first would compute it without the fee (122.75) and leave the fee unpaid after the call.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the late fee leaves period_late_fee = 0.00, so the payment is 112.27 + 0.00 + 0.48 + 10.00 = 122.75 instead of 134.75 (runner output 'skip prereq -> 122.75'), and the terminal ledger lacks the 12.00 late fee row; with the fee the balance ends at 5730.75 + 12.00 - 134.75 = 5608.00, without it at 5730.75 - 122.75 = 5608.00 but with a different ledger and a different payment row.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to pay what brings the card back into good standing; it never mentions a late fee or any charge owed. The only related line is passive and conditional: if the representative explains that a charge has to be put on first, he lets them go ahead.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: authorize_phone_payment_1fdda3b1 finds the card by its digits, creates the payment row and updates current_balance; it reads no fee and checks no statement, so it stays callable and writes faithfully before the late fee exists. post_missed_payment_late_fee_0b17ca39 likewise writes the fee row with no check.
